checklist.text: 90-day probation is complete; attendance record and any prior written Security Manager approval for an authorized absence are reviewed.
OJT-001 is complete, signed, and supported by live observed work.
PMC-T1-Core, PMC-T1-Gate, PMC-T1-Patrol, and PMC-T1-Base are complete and signed by a Lead or other authorized evaluator.
Evaluator dates, names, and underlying shift or training evidence support each competency signoff; gaps and rechecks are identified.
Identifies the current Gate Reference and follows the badge, red or denied read, and no-badge verification path under qualified direction.
Explains the limited T1 authority to verbally hold a driver pending Officer or Supervisor direction, promptly escalate, and never make an independent grant or denial.
Explains visitor verification through Base and vendor appointment/routing verification through the current program without inventing an exception.
Communicates calmly, keeps the lane safe, records who/what/when/outcome, and does not physically detain a driver who refuses to hold.
Completes observed patrols with safe positioning around forklifts, dock movement, vehicles, and restricted areas.
Recognizes an unsecured door, perimeter concern, maintenance issue, or unsafe behavior and gives a prompt factual report to Base and the Supervisor.
Understands planned patrol cycles, accurate logs, and documented reasons for a missed or delayed round; does not fabricate checkpoint activity.
Identifies the qualified Base officer's role in incident intake, radio traffic, camera monitoring, dispatch, and documentation; does not operate systems independently at T1.
Relays a clear location, nature of event, persons involved, time, and immediate hazards without guessing or assuming an outcome.
Explains when any officer may call 911 for a clear emergency and how to notify Base and the Supervisor.
Describes safe withdrawal and current EAP direction for fire or ammonia; no re-entry on a detector reading alone.
Provides complete post relief and pass-down, uses appropriate radio discipline, and makes truthful, timely log entries.
Demonstrates respectful direction, de-escalation, and awareness of when a confrontation must move to a qualified Officer or Supervisor.
Supervisor records observed strengths, development needs, recheck dates, and readiness for T2 independent post development.

scenarios.prompt:
A driver has no working badge and says Dispatch expects them. As a Trainee, explain your words and actions, how you hold for an Officer or Supervisor, and what you record. What if the driver refuses to wait?

Additional operational facts: The lane is filling. The driver says the delivery is urgent and asks you to wave the truck through while Dispatch sorts out the badge. You are the Trainee with a qualified Officer available by radio.
scenarios.title: Driver without a badge
scenarios.inject: The driver says they will drive around the lane control and asks for your name. What do you say and whom do you notify?

scenarios.prompt:
A visitor says they have an appointment but cannot be verified through the standard Base process. As a Trainee, explain how you seek qualified assistance and keep the visitor outside pending a decision.

Additional operational facts: The visitor identifies an employee they are meeting, but that employee has not answered Base's call. A nearby employee says they recognize the visitor and asks you to let them inside while they make another call.
scenarios.title: Visitor with unconfirmed appointment
scenarios.inject: The visitor asks to wait inside because of the weather. Explain the safe waiting arrangement and who can authorize access.

scenarios.prompt:
A badge reader shows red during a busy arrival period. What can you do as a Trainee to control the immediate situation, and who makes the access decision?

Additional operational facts: The person insists the badge worked yesterday. Vehicles are queued and a second officer is occupied at the opposite lane. You have the current Gate Reference, but the reason for the red read is not immediately clear.
scenarios.title: Denied badge in a busy lane
scenarios.inject: A manager from another department tells you to open the gate. Explain the Trainee's authority limit and the escalation you make.

scenarios.prompt:
While accompanying a qualified officer on patrol, you find a propped exterior door. Describe safe observations, radio notification, and factual documentation without assuming authority to clear the area alone.

Additional operational facts: You and the qualified patrol officer see an exterior door propped open near active truck movement. There is no visible person nearby, and the area beyond the doorway is not in your direct line of sight.
scenarios.title: Propped door on a supervised patrol
scenarios.inject: You hear movement inside before the qualified officer reaches the door. Explain where you stand, what you radio, and what you avoid doing alone.

scenarios.prompt:
At post relief, the outgoing officer mentions an unresolved alarm without a location or disposition. What facts do you ask for, and when do you involve the Lead or Supervisor before accepting the assignment?

Additional operational facts: The outgoing officer is leaving quickly and says only that the alarm was probably false. You have not been told when it occurred, where it happened, whether anyone responded, or what remains open.
scenarios.title: Incomplete alarm pass-down
scenarios.inject: The officer says, 'Just write resolved in the log so I can leave.' Explain the accurate handoff and when the Lead or Supervisor gets involved.

scenarios.prompt:
During a supervised patrol, a forklift approaches a pedestrian. Describe immediate safe warning, where you position yourself, whom you notify, and the facts to document.

Additional operational facts: During a supervised round, a forklift approaches a blind intersection while a pedestrian starts across. You are several steps away and cannot safely stop the equipment yourself.
scenarios.title: Forklift and pedestrian near miss
scenarios.inject: After the immediate hazard passes, the operator disputes what you saw. Explain how you record firsthand facts and whom you inform.

scenarios.prompt:
While observing at Base, you hear a report of an injury with an unclear location. Explain the information you relay, when 911 may be called, and why a qualified Base officer or Supervisor directs the response.

Additional operational facts: At Base familiarization, you hear 'someone is hurt in the warehouse' over the radio. The qualified Base officer is taking another urgent call; you do not yet know the exact location, injury type, or immediate hazards.
scenarios.title: Injury report with uncertain location
scenarios.inject: A second caller says the person may be unresponsive. Explain what you relay and whether a clear emergency permits an immediate 911 call.

scenarios.prompt:
During Base familiarization, a critical camera view fails. What information do you pass to the qualified Base officer and Supervisor, and what system actions are outside Trainee authority?

Additional operational facts: A critical camera image goes black while the qualified Base officer is coordinating a separate incident. You can see a system warning but do not know whether recording has stopped.
scenarios.title: Critical camera view unavailable
scenarios.inject: Another employee asks you to change system settings to restore the view. Explain what you report, how you preserve the time, and the authority boundary.

scenarios.prompt:
A driver presents information that conflicts with the current Gate Reference. Explain how a Trainee holds for a qualified Officer or Supervisor and avoids making an independent exception.

Additional operational facts: The paperwork, driver name, and expected delivery details do not agree. The driver says Receiving can fix the record after entry, and a line of trucks is backing up behind them.
scenarios.title: Gate information conflicts with reference
scenarios.inject: A warehouse employee says the driver is familiar. Explain what a Trainee may do to maintain a safe hold and who resolves the discrepancy.

scenarios.prompt:
A coworker asks you to omit a required log entry because the shift is busy. Explain how you make a truthful entry and escalate pressure to change the record.

Additional operational facts: A coworker asks you to leave out an access delay so that the shift report looks clean. You saw the delay yourself and have enough information to make a factual time-stamped record.
scenarios.title: Pressure to omit a log entry
scenarios.inject: The coworker says the Supervisor asked them to handle it informally. Explain how you verify direction without changing facts or accusing anyone.

checklist.text: PMC-Officer v2.0 is complete with authorized Lead signoff, overall section average at least 2.5, and no required item scored 1.
Security Manager verifies at least 98% documentation accuracy across logs, reports, and Gate paperwork during the preceding 60 days.
Sixty-day record shows sustained documented solo patrol activity, with operational reasons entered for missed or delayed cycles.
No active Step 2 Written Warning or above exists during the applicable review period; any lesser concern is documented for Manager consideration.
Independent Gate, Patrol, and Base qualifications are verified by observed performance and the applicable signed post records.
Applies the current Gate Reference for employee, driver, visitor, and vendor access, including denied or red reads and no-badge cases.
Verifies visitors through Base and inbound vendors through the current appointment and dock-routing program; escalates unresolved exceptions.
Checks designated outbound Gate Passes for PWADC/Pig, Purity, Arka Express, Mayfield, and Marvin Keller without routinely stopping other third-party trucks.
For PWADC/Pig exit, verifies driver badge and compares truck, trailer, and seal identifiers with the pass.
Returns a designated truck with a pass discrepancy to Dispatch without holding it in the Gate lane or taking over load-release decisions.
Conducts genuine perimeter and interior rounds with situational awareness around traffic, forklifts, active docks, and restricted areas.
Identifies and reports access, safety, maintenance, seal, or apparent cargo concerns with location and factual details.
Coordinates dock-area concerns with Base, the Supervisor, and Dispatch or warehouse personnel without performing a separate Dock/Crosswalk post or release inspection.
Documents completed, delayed, and missed patrol activity accurately and preserves required post coverage.
Operates Base independently when authorized: monitors active views, handles intake, logs accurately, and maintains radio communication.
Dispatches within Base officer authority, seeks Supervisor direction when required, and calls 911 immediately when emergency services are clearly needed.
Bookmarks relevant footage with at least 30 seconds before and after the event and preserves event times and evidence chain; does not export video below Lead authority.
Reports critical camera or system failures promptly to the Security Manager through the current notification chain.
Produces independent incident reports and witness statements with complete facts, chronology, required sections, and attributed evidence references.
Separates direct observation, reported information, and labeled professional opinion; corrects records without changing another person's factual account.
Applies the current EAP to fire, ammonia, injury, spill, weather, and access emergencies within training and authority.
Shows sound routine access and safety judgment, de-escalates basic disagreement, and escalates threats, posturing, or persistent noncompliance.
Coordinates a complete handoff across Gate, Patrol, Base, and shift change while preserving qualified Gate and Base relief.

scenarios.prompt:
A known employee receives a denied badge read in a busy lane. Explain the current Gate Reference check, safe lane control, decision authority, Base escalation if unresolved, and documentation.

Additional operational facts: The employee says they need to clock in and claims the reader has failed before. The Gate Reference does not yet explain the denied read, and inbound traffic is rising.
scenarios.title: Denied employee badge at Gate
scenarios.inject: A department supervisor says the employee is scheduled. Explain the authorized verification, the safe lane action, and the record you make.

scenarios.prompt:
A PWADC / Pig driver presents a Gate Pass whose trailer or seal number does not match. Explain badge and pass checks, routing the truck back to Dispatch, and what Security records without reconciling the load.

Additional operational facts: A PWADC/Pig driver badges for exit. The pass lists a different seal number than the trailer displays. The driver says Dispatch already knows and asks you to fix the number by hand so the line keeps moving.
scenarios.title: Mismatched PWADC Gate Pass
scenarios.inject: Dispatch is occupied and the driver says they will leave anyway. Explain your Security role, the return routing, and the notification.

scenarios.prompt:
While authorized at Base, a fire alarm activates. Describe immediate EAP and 911 decisions, notifications, radio traffic, log entries, and qualified coverage of Base.

Additional operational facts: You are the qualified Base officer when the fire signal activates. A warehouse employee calls and says they smell smoke, while radio traffic from Gate requests an unrelated badge verification.
scenarios.title: Fire alarm while operating Base
scenarios.inject: The first responding officer reports no visible fire. Explain how new reports affect the EAP response, communications, and qualified Base coverage.

scenarios.prompt:
On solo patrol you notice an unfamiliar vehicle by a perimeter access point. Explain your safe observations, Base and Supervisor notifications, and factual record.

Additional operational facts: During an independent round you see an unfamiliar parked vehicle near a perimeter access point. A person is beside it, and you cannot confirm from your location whether they have entered a restricted area.
scenarios.title: Vehicle near perimeter access
scenarios.inject: The person begins moving toward the fence. Explain safe observation distance, radio information, Supervisor direction, and factual documentation.

scenarios.prompt:
A visitor claims a supervisor approved access but the standard Base verification has not confirmed it. Explain how you hold or deny entry under the current Gate Reference without inventing an exception.

Additional operational facts: The visitor names a warehouse supervisor who is unavailable for verification. Another department employee says the supervisor would approve it and asks you to accept their assurance.
scenarios.title: Visitor claims verbal approval
scenarios.inject: The visitor becomes loud and a second visitor arrives behind them. Describe safe traffic management, access decision authority, and escalation.

scenarios.prompt:
You observe possible smoke in a warehouse area while Gate traffic continues. Explain safe withdrawal and fire procedure, who receives the report, and how you avoid leaving Gate without qualified relief.

Additional operational facts: While working Gate you notice a possible smoke condition near a warehouse entrance. You cannot identify its source and the qualified relief officer is not yet on scene.
scenarios.title: Possible smoke with ongoing Gate traffic
scenarios.inject: A second employee reports an odor of burning. Explain the emergency action, 911/EAP judgment, Gate control, and how you obtain qualified relief.

scenarios.prompt:
An inbound vendor presents an email appointment after hours. Describe verification through the current vendor program, routing, access decision, and escalation if authorization remains unclear.

Additional operational facts: A vendor shows a forwarded email with a time and door number, but the current appointment program does not yet confirm the load. The driver wants to park inside while a warehouse contact is reached.
scenarios.title: Vendor's after-hours appointment
scenarios.inject: A warehouse worker recognizes the carrier but does not have the required verification. Explain routing, authorization, and documentation.

scenarios.prompt:
An injury is reported while Patrol is on another assignment. As the authorized Base officer, explain emergency call, notifications and dispatch within your authority, and what you ask the Supervisor to decide.

Additional operational facts: You are the authorized Base officer. A rover reports an employee injury at a dock but cannot yet describe how serious it is. Gate is requesting an access decision at the same time.
scenarios.title: Injury while Base has competing work
scenarios.inject: The rover now reports severe pain and loss of sensation. Reprioritize life safety, radio traffic, responders, Gate hold, and Supervisor notification.

scenarios.prompt:
Another department requests video of a possible incident. Explain bookmarking with at least 30 seconds before and after, preserving the request and event times, and who may authorize or perform an export.

Additional operational facts: A department manager requests a video clip of a possible incident. You locate the event while assigned to Base, but the manager wants a copy before the shift ends.
scenarios.title: Request for incident video
scenarios.inject: A second caller gives a different event time. Explain the time check, bookmark range, request log, evidence protection, and Lead export boundary.

scenarios.prompt:
A patrol alarm arrives while a vehicle queue builds. Explain your own assigned-post actions, prompt coordination with Base and the Supervisor, and the need for qualified Gate and Base relief.

Additional operational facts: An alarm requires attention during an active vehicle queue. You are at your assigned post, and the nearest officer is approaching a break. You do not know whether qualified Gate or Base relief is available.
scenarios.title: Patrol alarm and Gate queue
scenarios.inject: A warehouse employee asks you to leave immediately to inspect the alarm. Explain coordination, post coverage, and who decides competing assignments.

scenarios.prompt:
Two shift records conflict about an access event. Explain how you preserve each original account, verify times and facts, and submit a correction with attribution.

Additional operational facts: Two officers describe the same access event with different times and different accounts of who granted authorization. A supervisor wants one clean report for review.
scenarios.title: Conflicting shift records
scenarios.inject: One officer asks you to rewrite their entry to match the other. Explain how you preserve original accounts and make a traceable, attributed correction.

scenarios.prompt:
A junior officer repeatedly overlooks a hazard. Explain immediate safety notification and factual coaching within T2 authority, including when the Lead or Supervisor must address performance.

Additional operational facts: A junior officer fails to notice an obstructed emergency exit while accompanying you. You point it out; later in the shift the same officer again walks past an obvious safety concern.
scenarios.title: Repeatedly missed hazard
scenarios.inject: The officer says you are acting like a Supervisor. Explain the immediate safety response, factual coaching, and escalation within T2 authority.

scenarios.prompt:
An ammonia alarm sounds near your patrol area. Explain withdrawal, 911 and notifications under the EAP, how you keep others away, and why a detector reading alone cannot authorize re-entry.

Additional operational facts: You are near the reported area when an ammonia-related alarm activates. An employee says it is likely a sensor issue, and no visible cloud is apparent from your safe location.
scenarios.title: Ammonia alarm on patrol
scenarios.inject: Another report describes a strong odor or visible vapor. Explain how you update the EAP response, keep others away, and avoid unauthorized re-entry.

scenarios.prompt:
Severe weather information arrives during post relief. Describe your handoff, radio and log facts, and how you confirm qualified coverage without changing assignments on your own.

Additional operational facts: A severe weather notice arrives while Gate and Base are changing officers. The incoming qualified Base officer has not received the notice, and one patrol assignment is late.
scenarios.title: Severe weather at post relief
scenarios.inject: A radio caller asks which area to evacuate. Explain current EAP direction, handoff facts, qualified coverage, and who directs an assignment change.

scenarios.prompt:
While authorized at Base, you see an unknown person entering a restricted area. Explain safe dispatch within Base authority, Supervisor notification, event bookmarking, and factual documentation.

Additional operational facts: An active camera shows an unknown person moving toward a restricted area. You are the qualified Base officer and have only a partial description; another radio channel has routine traffic.
scenarios.title: Unknown person in a restricted area
scenarios.inject: The person disappears from that camera. Explain dispatch within Base authority, evidence preservation, Supervisor updates, and escalation.

scenarios.prompt:
You hear a post instruction has changed but have not seen the controlled update. Explain how you verify current direction and communicate it without inventing policy.

Additional operational facts: A coworker says a Gate step changed today, but you have not seen the approved update. A driver arrives with a case that would be handled differently if the change is real.
scenarios.title: Unverified post instruction change
scenarios.inject: The coworker says everyone has already adopted the new practice. Explain how to verify controlling direction and communicate an unresolved case.

scenarios.prompt:
A third-party outbound truck requests release while a designated Gate Pass check is in progress. Explain which carriers receive routine outbound checks and how you keep the lane moving without a new routine stop.

Additional operational facts: A designated carrier is receiving its required Gate Pass check while a third-party outbound truck queues behind it. Someone suggests you begin checking every outbound truck to be safe.
scenarios.title: Outbound truck during designated pass check
scenarios.inject: The third-party driver protests the delay. Explain which carriers have designated checks, lane control, and any reason to escalate an actual concern.

scenarios.prompt:
During patrol you find an apparent seal or cargo concern by a dock. Explain observations and notifications to Base, the Supervisor, and responsible Dispatch or warehouse staff; identify who owns load and release decisions.

Additional operational facts: During an independent patrol you observe an apparent seal discrepancy near an active dock. You do not know whether Dispatch is already addressing it, and the trailer is preparing to leave.
scenarios.title: Seal or cargo concern by a dock
scenarios.inject: A warehouse employee asks you to release the load because they are behind schedule. Explain the factual notification chain and decision owner.

checklist.text: Signed post records confirm independent Gate, Patrol, and Base proficiency; post mastery was established before this leadership review.
Sixty-day review shows sound independent operational judgment with minimal leadership reversals and specific supporting examples.
Independent Base proficiency is verified by a Lead or above, and Lead-level technical readiness is verified by the Security Manager or designee.
Manager/designee verifies surveillance across active camera positions, forensic review and authorized clip extraction, multi-channel dispatch, and accurate Base logs.
Lead or above confirms objective review of Officer reports for factual gaps, chronology errors, required sections, and unsupported conclusions.
Demonstrates success mentoring Trainees to solo proficiency through observed training and documented outcomes.
Explains the Lead's primary FTO responsibility, plans training across Gate, Patrol, and Base, and maintains training continuity across shifts.
Evaluates live competency fairly, withholds unsupported signoffs, records evidence, and uses a Senior Officer as supporting FTO when authorized.
Provides specific, respectful feedback and rechecks a gap without lowering the qualification standard to solve a staffing shortage.
Maintains professional boundaries and impartiality when assessing peers, friends, or officers with performance concerns.
Coordinates routine relief and coverage with the Supervisor, keeping Gate and Base staffed by qualified personnel and patrol activity documented.
Prioritizes life safety, clear radio updates, 911 when needed, and assistance to the Supervisor and incident commander without claiming their authority.
Recognizes the difference between Lead operational direction and formal Acting Supervisor activation by explicit Supervisor communication for a prolonged absence.
On a formal Acting Supervisor assignment, records activation and duration, manages only delegated operational needs, and notifies the Security Manager if the absence extends.
Obtains Security Manager direction before formal counseling, sending an employee home for conduct/performance, or approving overtime; never self-authorizes promotion or pay.
Coordinates access and designated Gate Pass concerns without taking over Dispatch or warehouse cargo release decisions.
Reviews Officer incident reports for the 5 W's, sequence, factual support, required sections, and unlabeled opinion before Supervisor review.
Preserves original accounts and corrections with attribution and gives complete incident and shift handoffs.
Demonstrates appropriate video bookmarking, source preservation, Lead-level authorized export, recipient controls, and transfer documentation.
Monitors critical Base equipment and camera issues, documents impact, and escalates outages through the proper chain.
Models calm decisions, factual communication, and constructive coaching during concurrent calls or changing conditions.
Supervisor recommendation identifies observed leadership evidence, each development gap, the verbal scenario grades, and any recheck.
Security Manager interview is completed in person or live conversation, dated, recorded, and rated before final T4 approval.
Security Manager reviews signed qualifications, the 60-day record, report review ability, Base technical verification, and the interview before approving or deferring promotion.

scenarios.title: The Driver Who “Comes Here Every Week”
scenarios.prompt: You are supporting Gate operations. A driver arrives with a delivery and says he comes to PWADC every week. His company is recognized, but the information presented does not match what Security expects for the delivery. The driver says, “Receiving knows me. Just let me through and I’ll straighten it out at the dock.” Receiving is not answering immediately. Three trucks are waiting behind him and the driver is becoming irritated. A warehouse employee says, “He’s probably fine. Just send him in.” Walk through what you do.

scenarios.title: Safety Violation That Will Not Stop
scenarios.prompt: While on warehouse patrol, you observe a forklift operator repeatedly entering intersections without following the required internal safety practice. You address the operator professionally. The behavior continues. You notify the appropriate warehouse supervisor. Ten minutes later, you observe the same behavior again. The warehouse supervisor says, “I already talked to him. Don’t worry about it.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Coverage Starts Falling Apart
scenarios.prompt: You are the T3 Senior Officer on duty. One rover calls out. Another officer is due for a break. Gate traffic is unusually heavy. BASE advises that an officer is needed for a warehouse issue. The Security Supervisor is temporarily occupied and says, “Handle the rotations and keep everybody covered. Call me if you actually need me.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: BASE Gets Hit From Four Directions
scenarios.prompt: You are operating BASE. Within approximately one minute: Gate calls requesting verification of an individual; a rover reports an employee injury; another officer radios about a suspicious vehicle; and a warehouse manager calls asking for immediate camera review of an earlier incident. Walk through your priorities.

scenarios.title: Ammonia Report Changes Mid-Incident
scenarios.prompt: BASE receives a call from an employee near the cold side: “I smell ammonia. I don’t see anything, but it’s strong.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Fire Alarm, Then Conflicting Information
scenarios.prompt: BASE receives a fire-related alarm from a warehouse area. An officer checks the vicinity and reports, “I don’t see fire. I don’t see smoke.” A warehouse employee then calls from the same general area and says, “Something smells like it’s burning.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: The Officer Who Challenges You in Front of Everyone
scenarios.prompt: You direct an officer to rotate from Patrol to Gate to maintain coverage. In front of two other officers, the officer responds, “You’re not my Supervisor. You’re just trying to act important because you want T4.” The officer refuses to move. What do you do?

scenarios.title: Supervisor Gives a Questionable Shortcut
scenarios.prompt: A busy Security Supervisor tells you, “We’re backed up. Skip part of the normal verification process for these next few drivers. Receiving is expecting a bunch of them.” You believe the instruction conflicts with established Gate procedure. What do you do?

scenarios.title: Missing Person During Evacuation
scenarios.prompt: An evacuation has been initiated. Department accountability reports one employee missing. Another employee says, “I saw him go back inside because he left his keys.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Injury With Pressure to Keep It Quiet
scenarios.prompt: An employee reports an injury. The employee’s supervisor says, “He’s fine. He doesn’t want to make a big deal out of it. Don’t call anyone and don’t write anything.” The employee then tells Security, “Actually, I do want to be checked out.” What happens next?

scenarios.title: It Is Probably Nothing
scenarios.prompt: BASE receives an alarm associated with a warehouse area. An officer checks the general area and reports, “I don’t see anything.” A minute later, an employee calls and says, “I smell something burning over here.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Ammonia Odor Becomes a Cloud
scenarios.prompt: An employee near the cold side radios BASE: “I smell ammonia pretty strong.” No visible cloud has been reported. What do you do?

scenarios.title: Serious Employee Injury
scenarios.prompt: A rover reports, “Employee fell from a dock area. He’s awake and talking.” What information do you need and what do you do?

scenarios.title: Missing Employee During Evacuation
scenarios.prompt: An evacuation is underway. Area supervisors report headcounts. One department reports, “We are missing one employee.” A coworker says, “I think he went back for his truck keys.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Power Failure Becomes More Than a Power Failure
scenarios.prompt: The facility loses power. Emergency lighting is functioning. Several people begin calling BASE asking when power will return. What do you prioritize?

scenarios.title: Bomb Threat Call
scenarios.prompt: BASE answers the phone. The caller states, “There’s a bomb in your building.” What do you do?

scenarios.title: Two Emergencies at Once
scenarios.prompt: While BASE is coordinating an employee medical emergency, Gate reports a vehicle attempting to follow another vehicle through controlled entry. A fire alarm appears from another part of the building. The Supervisor is responding to the medical call and is not immediately available by radio. Walk through your first 60 seconds.
